column1: indistinct§An indistinct memory is not the same as a false one.§**模糊**的记忆与虚假的记忆不是一回事。
individuality§Individuality in handwriting is what makes forgery hard.§笔迹的**个性**正是伪造之所以困难的原因。
indivisible§The problem is indivisible: solve half and you have solved none.§这个问题**不可分割**：解决一半等于没解决。
indolence§A week of indolence after a long project is well earned.§长项目之后**懒散**一周是应得的。
indomitable§An indomitable hedge came back three times after cutting.§这道**顽强**的树篱被砍了三次又长了回来。
inducement§The only inducement offered was a better chair.§提供的唯一**诱因**是一把更好的椅子。
induction§Her induction into the society took four minutes.§她**加入该协会的仪式**用了四分钟。
indulge§Indulge me for one more paragraph and the point will be clear.§**再容我写一段**，要点就清楚了。
indulgence§The whole chapter is an indulgence and the book is better for it.§整章都是**纵情之作**，这本书却因此更好。
indulgent§An indulgent review of a friend's book helps nobody.§对朋友的书作**宽纵**的评论对谁都没好处。
industrious§Industrious does not mean effective, though we often confuse them.§**勤奋**不等于有效，尽管我们常常混淆两者。
ineffable§He gave up trying to describe it and called it ineffable.§他放弃了描述，索性说它**难以言表**。
ineffectual§An ineffectual chair lets the loudest person decide.§**无能**的主席会让嗓门最大的人做主。
inefficacious§An inefficacious remedy that does no harm still wastes time.§**无效**但无害的疗法仍然浪费时间。
inept§He was inept with people and formidable with numbers.§他**不擅长**与人打交道，对数字却极为在行。
ineptitude§Ineptitude at the top is expensive in ways that never appear in accounts.§高层的**无能**所付出的代价，账目上永远看不到。
inert§The committee was inert until a deadline appeared.§委员会一直**毫无动静**，直到出现了截止日期。
inescapable§The smell of the tannery was inescapable within a mile.§一英里之内都**躲不开**制革厂的气味。
inevitability§Nothing has the air of inevitability like a decision already taken.§没有什么比已经作出的决定更显得**理所当然**。
inevitably§The correction inevitably reaches fewer readers than the error.§更正到达的读者，**必然**比错误少。
inexorable§Erosion is inexorable and, on a human scale, invisible.§侵蚀**不可阻挡**，在人的尺度上却看不见。
inexplicable§The most inexplicable part is why nobody wrote it down.§**最难解释**的是为什么没人把它记下来。
infallible§He treated his own memory as infallible and it was not.§他把自己的记忆当作**绝对可靠**，事实并非如此。
infamous§An infamous typo survived four editions.§一个**臭名昭著**的印刷错误熬过了四个版本。
infatuation§Infatuation with a method is the enemy of a good result.§**迷恋**一种方法是好结果的敌人。
infelicity§One infelicity in a translation is forgivable; a page is not.§译文里一处**不当**可以原谅，整页就不行。
inferiority§The inferiority of the copy is visible only beside the original.§副本的**低劣**只有与原件并置时才看得出。
infighting§Infighting is invisible from outside and obvious in the minutes.§**内斗**从外面看不见，会议记录里却一目了然。
inflammatory§The word is inflammatory and the fact behind it is dull.§这个词很**煽情**，它背后的事实却很平淡。
inflexibility§Inflexibility about small things buys you nothing.§在小事上的**僵硬**什么也换不来。
inflexible§An inflexible rule applied to a flexible world produces absurdity.§**僵硬**的规则套用在灵活的世界上会产生荒谬。
informal§An informal register suits the subject better than a formal one.§**非正式的**语体比正式语体更适合这个题材。
infrequent§Infrequent visits made every visit an occasion.§来访**稀少**，使得每次来访都成了大事。
infusion§An infusion of the dried leaves was drunk for fever.§用这种干叶**泡的茶**被用来退烧。
ingenue§The ingenue in the third act is the only honest character.§第三幕里那个**天真少女**是唯一诚实的角色。
ingenuous§An ingenuous account is worth more than a polished one.§一份天真**坦白的**叙述胜过一份精心润色的。
inhibit§Nothing inhibits a discussion like a senior person taking notes.§没有什么比一位上级在记笔记更能**抑制**讨论。
inhibition§Loss of inhibition is not the same as gain of insight.§放下**拘束**并不等于获得洞见。
inhospitable§The room was inhospitable in a way no furniture could fix.§这个房间的**不宜居**，是任何家具都补救不了的。
inimitable§Her inimitable hand is why the letters can be dated at all.§正因为她那**无法模仿**的笔迹，这些信才得以断代。
initiate§He was initiated into the trade by watching for a year.§他靠看了一年，**被引入了这门行当**。
innocence§There is an innocence in the early drawings that later work loses.§早期素描中有一种后来作品失去的**天真**。
innocuous§An innocuous phrase in one country is an insult in another.§在一个国家**无害的**说法，在另一个国家就是侮辱。
innovation§Innovation in the archive means a better box.§档案工作里的**创新**，就是做出更好的盒子。
innovative§Innovative and reliable rarely appear in the same year.§**创新**与可靠很少出现在同一年。
innovator§The innovator's notebooks are more interesting than the product.§这位**创新者**的笔记本比产品更有意思。
inordinate§An inordinate share of the budget went to the entrance.§预算中**过大**的一部分花在了入口上。
insatiable§An insatiable market for the fish emptied the bay.§对这种鱼**永不满足**的市场需求把海湾掏空了。
inscrutable§The machine's error message was inscrutable and possibly a joke.§这台机器的错误提示**令人费解**，也许是个玩笑。
insecurity§Insecurity, not arrogance, explains most of his behaviour.§解释他大部分行为的是**不安全感**，而不是傲慢。
insensitive§The instrument is insensitive below a certain temperature.§这台仪器在某一温度以下就**不灵敏**了。
inseparable§For twenty years the two names were inseparable in print.§二十年里，这两个名字在出版物上**密不可分**。
insidious§Insidious is the right word for damp.§用“**隐伏**”来形容潮气正合适。
insightful§Insightful and correct are not the same thing.§**有洞察力**与正确并不是一回事。
insignificant§Statistically insignificant does not mean unimportant.§统计上**不显著**并不意味着不重要。
insinuate§He insinuated himself into a committee that had not invited him.§他**钻进**了一个并未邀请他的委员会。
insinuation§An insinuation is designed to be deniable.§**暗讽**的设计就是为了可以否认。
insipid§An insipid summary of a fierce book does it no favours.§一篇**平淡**的摘要对一本猛烈的书毫无帮助。
insistence§His insistence on the old spelling was not eccentricity.§他**坚持**旧拼法并非古怪。
insistent§The insistent question is the one that gets answered.§**坚持**不懈的问题才是能得到回答的问题。
insolence§What reads as insolence in print was probably fatigue.§文字里读来像**傲慢**的，很可能是疲惫。
insolent§An insolent letter was framed and hung in the office.§一封**无礼**的信被裱起来挂在了办公室。
insolvent§Insolvent by June, the firm was trading again by autumn.§六月已**资不抵债**，到秋天这家公司又开始营业了。
instantaneous§The change is not instantaneous; it takes about four seconds.§这种变化不是**瞬间的**，大约要四秒。
instigate§Nobody would admit to having instigated the change.§没人肯承认是自己**发起**了这次变动。
instinctive§An instinctive response is worth examining, not trusting.§**本能的**反应值得审视，而不是信任。
instructive§It is instructive to read the two drafts side by side.§把两份草稿并排读很**有教益**。
instructor§A good instructor says less in the second lesson than the first.§好的**教练**第二堂课说的话比第一堂少。
